summary: This PR wires src/app/api/ai/orchestrate/route.ts through Mother Router's end_user_org scope (Gateway G05) instead of calling orchestra-model-resolver.ts's resolveModelConfig() directly, giving that route a real audit-logged, policy-overridable resolution path where none existed before; the change is additive, isolated to one route plus mother-router.ts's new optional resolvedConfig field, preserves the existing BYO-precedence and audit-log contract (verified by reading resolveModel/computeEndUserOrgResolution/logRoutingDecision directly, not just trusting the self-report), keeps the enforcePolicy() guardrail marker required by scripts/check-guardrail-presence.mjs intact, does not touch migrations/auth/payment/billing/RLS paths or .github/workflows/**, and adds 4 new unit tests for the added resolvedConfig behavior. One real but currently-dormant correctness bug was found in computeEndUserOrgResolution's package-override branch: resolvedConfig is built via `{ ...baseline, provider: override.provider, model: override.model, apiKey: overrideApiKey }`, which overrides provider/model/apiKey but silently carries over baseline.fallback -- a fallback chain computed by orchestra-model-resolver.ts's platformFallbackFor() for the ORIGINAL (pre-override) provider/model, not for the override's. Since computeEndUserOrgResolution is a synchronous pure function it cannot call the async platformFallbackFor() itself to recompute this. Today this is unreachable in production (grep confirms no seeded ai_routing_policies row anywhere in the repo names a preferredModelByPackage for the end_user_org scope, so getActivePolicy() returns null and the override branch never fires), so it does not block this additive, low-blast-radius tier1 change from merging -- but it will silently misfire the moment someone activates a real package-routing policy for this scope (the LLM failover call would retry against a provider/model pairing computed for the wrong primary), which is exactly the next step this phase sets up. Recommend a fast-follow to either recompute the fallback for the override provider/model inside resolveModel()'s end_user_org branch (async, outside the pure function) before calling computeEndUserOrgResolution, or explicitly document/strip the stale fallback as unsafe-to-use until fixed.
issues: computeEndUserOrgResolution's package-override branch (mother-router.ts) builds resolvedConfig by spreading baseline and only overriding provider/model/apiKey, leaving resolvedConfig.fallback as whatever orchestra-model-resolver.ts's platformFallbackFor() computed for the pre-override baseline provider/model -- a mismatched failover target once callLLMJsonCached uses modelConfig.fallback in orchestrate/route.ts. Currently dormant (no active ai_routing_policies row for end_user_org exists anywhere in the repo yet) but will misfire on the first real package-override policy + primary-call failure. Non-blocking for this tier1 merge; recommend a targeted follow-up fix.
